items.content_text:
Black communities are not a monolith. We have different experiences, generations, values, and relationships with politics that shape how we engage.
 Building Black political power requires more than asking people to vote. It requires understanding why some people participate, why others feel disconnected, and what people need to see change is possible.
 Our power grows when we listen to each other, understand our differences, and organize from where people are.

As we've had an influx of door-to-door solicitors recently, we'd like to share an important reminder with our community.
 At this time, Aptive Environmental is the only company with an active solicitor's permit issued by the Town of Signal Mountain.
 If someone comes to your door selling products or services, you have the right to ask to see their Town-issued permit. A valid permit will:
 * Include the Town of Signal Mountain seal as a watermark.
 * Display a photo of the solicitor.
 If a solicitor cannot produce a valid permit, or if something simply doesn't feel right, please contact the Signal Mountain Police Department's non-emergency number at (423) 886-2123.
 As always, if you see something, say something. We'd much rather investigate a concern than have someone take advantage of our community!

items.content_text:
Official development assistance (ODA) to sub-Saharan Africa and least developed countries is projected to decline again in 2026.
 An #OECD policy brief projects a third consecutive year of decline in bilateral ODA to sub-Saharan Africa and least developed countries, bringing support to its lowest level since the early 2000s.
 ➡️ Bilateral ODA to sub-Saharan Africa could decline by 11.6% in 2026
 ➡️ Least developed countries could see a decline of 10.9% 
 The projected declines follow significant reductions in 2025, when ODA to sub-Saharan Africa and least developed countries fell by 26.3% and 25.8% respectively.
 The policy brief also notes that many of the countries most exposed to the current contraction rely on a limited number of providers for development finance, increasing their vulnerability to reductions in ODA.
 Multilateral ODA is also projected to decline in 2026, limiting the ability of international organisations to help offset reductions in bilateral aid. 
 Read the policy brief: https://brnw.ch/21x4HUe
 #ODA2026 #OECDdevelopment

The event brought together organizations from across our community that are working every day to expand access, remove barriers, and create opportunities for individuals with disabilities.

From learning about Harrison Bay State Park's Access 2030 initiative to connecting with organizations like Special Olympics, the National Federation of the Blind, Partnership for Deaf Services, the American Job Center, and many others, the day highlighted the incredible impact that collaboration can have across our region.

Thank you to the City of Chattanooga Mayor's Council on Disability for bringing our community together to celebrate the progress we've made and to continue advancing accessibility and inclusion for all.

At SETD, we're proud to support initiatives that strengthen our communities and improve quality of life for the people we serve!

 🥣 Read cereal boxes together over breakfast.

 Because families are a child’s first teachers and every moment is a chance to learn. 🌟

Exploring Downtown: Bluff View Art District
 Perched above the Tennessee River, Bluff View Art District is one of Downtown Chattanooga's most beloved destinations, known for its galleries, gardens, restaurants, and scenic overlooks. But long before it became an arts district, Bluff View was one of Chattanooga's most prestigious neighborhoods. In the late 1800s and early 1900s, many of the city's wealthiest families had homes here, including George Thomas Hunter, heir to the Coca-Cola bottling fortune.
 By the late 20th century, many of Bluff View's historic properties had fallen into disrepair. In the early 1990s, Dr. Charles and Mary Portera changed the neighborhood's fate by purchasing and restoring many of its buildings, with the goal of creating an art district to complement the nearby art museums. In 1992, they opened the River Gallery and by the end of the 1990s, the Porteras had opened multiple businesses across the district, all united by landscaped gardens, walkways, and beautiful courtyards. 
 Today, the Bluff View Art District is one of Downtown Chattanooga's signature destinations, where history, art, and architecture come together in one walkable neighborhood.
 Photo Credit: Bluff View Art District, Chattanooga Tourism Co.

In the late 1800s and early 1900s, many of the city's wealthiest families had homes here, including George Thomas Hunter, heir to the Coca-Cola bottling fortune.
By the late 20th century, many of Bluff View's historic properties had fallen into disrepair. In the early 1990s, Dr. Charles and Mary Portera changed the neighborhood's fate by purchasing and restoring many of its buildings, with the goal of creating an art district to complement the nearby art museums. In 1992, they opened the River Gallery and by the end of the 1990s, the Porteras had opened multiple businesses across the district, all united by landscaped gardens, walkways, and beautiful courtyards.
Today, the Bluff View Art District is one of Downtown Chattanooga's signature destinations, where history, art, and architecture come together in one walkable neighborhood.

📍 A Great First Step for Downtown Red Bank!
 On Friday, July 31, the Tennessee Downtowns Steering Committee held its first official meeting, marking an exciting milestone in Red Bank's downtown revitalization journey.
 The day began with a walking tour of downtown, where committee members, project partners, and City staff had the opportunity to visit with local business owners and experience firsthand the strengths, opportunities, and unique character that make our downtown special.
 A special thank you to All About the Bride & Ivory HydroSpa, Vintage and More, Capitol Barbershop, and Bread and Butter for taking the time to visit with our group, provide business tours, and share your unique perspectives on doing business in Downtown Red Bank. Your insight and willingness to engage in the planning process will help shape the future of our downtown.
 Following the tour, the committee participated in a collaborative SWOT (Strengths, Weaknesses, Opportunities, and Threats) analysis, identifying priorities, opportunities, and the next steps that will help shape a vibrant, welcoming, and economically resilient downtown.
 This first official meeting represents the beginning of an exciting two-year journey that will build upon community input, strategic planning, and strong partnerships to create a shared vision for Downtown Red Bank.
 A special thank you to The Spritzeria for graciously hosting lunch and providing the perfect venue for the SWOT workshop. Your hospitality and investment in Downtown Red Bank are greatly appreciated.
 We would also like to extend our sincere appreciation to Frank Clark with the Tennessee Department of Economic and Community Development for his leadership, guidance, and commitment to helping communities like Red Bank build stronger, more vibrant downtowns. Your expertise and support are invaluable as we begin this transformative process.
 Finally, thank you to each member of the Tennessee Downtowns Steering Committee for your willingness to serve and invest your time, ideas, and passion into Red Bank's future. Together, we're laying out the foundation for a downtown that reflects our community's character while creating new opportunities for residents, businesses, and visitors alike.
 Stay tuned as we continue sharing updates throughout this exciting journey!
 #RedBankTN #TNDowntowns #DowntownRedBank #CommunityDevelopment #MainStreet #DowntownRevitalization #TNECD #BuildingCommunity

🔎 Where in Red Bank is Justin Headrick?
 Recently, Justin was spotted at the Red Bank Community Center working alongside Williams Plumbing to install a brand-new drinking fountain with a bottle-filling station! 💧
 This project is part of the Facilities Division's ongoing effort to provide filtered drinking water at every City facility, making it easier for residents and visitors to stay hydrated while reducing the use of single-use plastic bottles.
 Thank you to everyone involved in helping make Red Bank an even better place to live, work, and play! 👏

items.content_text:
Teamwork in action: CFD Special Operations assisted CHAPublicWorks Friday during repair operations for a sinkhole in downtown.
 Working together, crews entered the storm basin to remove a section of concrete that was restricting water flow. This collaborative effort will help improve drainage and support ongoing repairs while preventing further obstruction.
 Great coordination between agencies to help keep our city’s infrastructure functioning safely!

You're Invited to Celebrate with us in #EastRidgeTN! 🙌🏼
 After months of construction and renovations, we're excited to officially welcome the community back to the East Ridge Community Center!
 Join us on Saturday, August 22. 2026 as we celebrate the Community Center's Grand Re-Opening with a ribbon-cutting ceremony at beginning 11:00 AM, followed by an open house until 4:00 PM. 
 Bring the family, tour the renovated facility, meet our Parks and Recreation team, enjoy activities throughout the day, grab a bite to eat (while supplies last), and enter for a chance to win some great raffle prizes donated by local businesses. 
 This project represents the largest renovation to the Community Center since it opened in 1994. From the expanded gymnasium and updated facilities to improved accessibility and new spaces for future programming, we're excited to open the doors and show everyone what's new. 
 🗓️ Saturday, August 22, 2026 
 ✂️ Ribbon Cutting: 11:00am 
 ⛹🏻‍♀️ Open House: 11:00am until 4:00pm 
 We hope you'll come celebrate with us and see everything the new Community Center has to offer! 
 📍 East Ridge Community Center 
    1515 Tombras Avenue
     East Ridge, TN 37412 
 We can’t wait to see you there! 💙🧡🤍
